title: Governor of Vermont

context.text: Incumbent Republican Phil Scott is seeking a sixth two-year term; Vermont has no gubernatorial term limit. He was unopposed in the August 11, 2026 Republican primary.
Economist Amanda Janoo, a first-time candidate, won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary over Aly Richards, a former advocacy-group CEO, and also holds the Progressive Party line.

Three other candidates are on the printed ballot: June Goodband (Peace and Justice), Dean Roy (Freedom and Unity) and Brian Judd (independent). Constitution Party write-in Mark Grimek and write-ins David King and Bryan Ponnwitz have also declared; they are not profiled here.

candidates.name: Phil Scott
candidates.ballotNote: Seeking a sixth term; unopposed in the Republican primary.

summary.text: Phil Scott is the Republican Governor of Vermont, first elected in 2016. A longtime business owner from Barre, he served in the state Senate (2001–2011) and as lieutenant governor (2011–2017). In 2026 he vetoed bills on reference-based health-care pricing, energy facilities, school mental-health funding and public-employee union organizing, and signed an education-system reform bill.

background.text: Born in Barre, Vermont; B.S. from the University of Vermont; long-time business owner who set records at Thunder Road speedbowl.
Served in the Vermont Senate (Washington district) 2001–2011 and as the 81st lieutenant governor 2011–2017.
Elected governor in 2016 and re-elected four times since.

priorities.text: Making Vermont affordable and growing the tax base; describes his approach as pragmatic and incremental.
priorities.quote: We need to take care of what's before us. I'm willing to compromise, I'm willing to work together, but it's got to make sense for the average Vermonter

priorities.text: A package of tax reductions or credits, which he has not yet specified; says he would prefer not to raise taxes.
priorities.quote: I would prefer not to raise any taxes

positions.summary: Opposes Janoo's proposed income surcharge on high earners, arguing wealthy residents would leave.
positions.quote: You're raising a tax on a group that I don't think will pay it.

record.text: Vetoed S.190 (reference-based pricing and the Green Mountain Care Board) on June 16, 2026, saying its savings would exclude most payers while hospital revenue reductions would affect all Vermonters buying insurance.

Vetoed H.710 (defining electricity generating facilities) and H.817 (school mental health supports) on June 17, 2026; on H.817 he called a requirement to propose funding in his budget "a clear separation of powers violation."
Vetoed S.230 (fair employment practices) on June 18, 2026, saying it favored one union over another in Department of Corrections organizing.
Signed H.955, "An act relating to next steps in transforming Vermont's education system," and S.328 (housing and common interest communities) on June 18, 2026.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions are limited to what could be directly sourced; his campaign website was not loaded.

candidates.name: Amanda Janoo
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 2026 Democratic primary; also the Progressive Party candidate.

summary.text: Amanda Janoo is a first-time candidate and economist who has worked in economic development for the United Nations and with the Wellbeing Economy Alliance. She proposes higher taxes on top earners, second homes and large tech companies to fund free primary and preventive health care and reduce property taxes.

background.text: Political newcomer; has worked in economic development for the United Nations and in economic sustainability with the Wellbeing Economy Alliance.
Won the Democratic nomination in August 2026.

priorities.text: Raising revenue from high earners, second homes and large digital advertisers to fund free primary and preventive care and lower property taxes.
priorities.quote: Phil Scott's definition of affordability is tax cuts.

priorities.text: Program implementation and evaluation to determine what works.
priorities.quote: I've spent my career working in the executive branch of government

positions.summary: Proposes a 2% surcharge on personal income over $250,000 and an 8% surcharge over $500,000, plus higher rates on luxury second homes and a tax on large tech companies' digital ad revenue.
Would use surcharge revenue to fund free primary and preventive care for all Vermonters.

candidates.researchNotes: Her campaign website could not be located; she has held no public office, so no record.

candidates.name: June Goodband
candidates.ballotNote: Peace and Justice Party candidate; also ran for governor in 2024.

summary.text: June Goodband is the Peace and Justice Party candidate for governor and was the party's 2024 nominee. A reference listing describes her as a psychotherapist and progressive activist.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or public statements were found.

candidates.name: Brian Judd

summary.text: Brian Judd is an independent candidate for governor. A reference listing describes him as an actor and Navy veteran who ran for city council in 2021 and the state House in 2022.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or public statements were found.

candidates.name: Dean Roy

summary.text: Dean Roy is the Freedom and Unity Party candidate for governor, a party he created. The Associated Press (via Fortune) described him in March 2026 as a freshman at Stowe High School and the first candidate for governor under age 18 on Vermont's general-election ballot.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or policy statements were found; basic facts come from the Secretary of State's candidate list and AP coverage.
